title: Cross-Functional Career Compass: Onboarding, Tools & Perks Integration
author: Maya Patel
content:
Purpose
This playbook unifies three operational areas that are currently managed in separate spaces: new hire onboarding, role & ladder alignment, and access to internal tooling and perks. Its goal is to reduce first-30-day friction for contributors, shorten time-to-productivity, and make career movements (rotations, promotions, role changes) predictable and transparent for distributed teams.

Audience
- People Ops and Hiring Managers
- Team managers and IC mentors
- Engineering and Product platform leads who own tools and permissions
- New joiners and contributors planning role changes

Scope
Covers: role alignment to ladder levels, a repeatable 0–90-day onboarding timeline, the tooling access matrix for common roles, a benefits-to-life-stage mapping, and the operational runbook for role transitions. It does NOT replace team-level onboarding checklists or specialized compliance onboarding (e.g., onboarding for customers with restricted data).

Executive summary
- Target: fully provisioned and productive contributor within 72 hours for basic tools, 30 days for fully integrated role access, 90 days for role competency checkpoint.
- Ownership: People Ops maintains the playbook; team managers drive onboarding content and first-90-day mentorship plans.
- Measurement: track time-to-first-PR, time-to-first-customer-facing-task, and first-90-day retention. Quarterly review required.

1) 0–90 Day Onboarding Roadmap (standardized)
Intro: This timeline standardizes the most common activities teams must complete. Customize with team-specific tasks.
- Day 0 (before start)
  1. Welcome packet (People Ops): benefits summary, team contact list, starter reading.
  2. Provisioning request (auto): Okta, GitHub, G-Suite, Slack, Confluence, 1Password; request submitted to provisioning pipeline.
  3. Manager sends first-week agenda.
- Day 1–3
  1. Orientation session (People Ops): payroll, benefits enrollment, code of conduct, hybrid policies.
  2. Core access verification: login to Okta and Slack, verify 1Password vault, confirm GitHub repo access.
  3. First small commit exercise assigned by manager.
- Day 4–30
  1. Role-specific training modules (team): onboarding checklist completion, architecture walkthrough, shadowing sessions.
  2. Tools deep-dive: observability dashboard read-only access, dev environment build, CI run.
  3. 30-day 1:1: manager and mentor review progress and blockers.
- Day 31–90
  1. Ownership of a small project (deliverable with PO/manager acceptance).
  2. Peer feedback collection and career checkpoint preparation.
  3. 90-day career checkpoint: rubric review and next-step career plan.

2) Role Alignment & Ladder Checkpoints
Purpose: make promotions, rotations, and hiring bands consistent across teams. Use competency-based checkpoints rather than tenure.
- Key ladder bands (summary): Associate IC, IC2, Senior IC, Staff/Lead, Principal/Director (manager tracks separate).
- Checkpoint cadence: promotable if candidate meets 3 of 5 rubric categories at the next band and has delivered at least one cross-team impact in the prior 12 months.

Competency rubric (summary table)
Title | Technical Craft | Product Impact | Communication | Ownership | Mentorship
------|----------------|----------------|---------------|----------|-----------
IC2   | Solid feature-level design | Clear feature delivery | Clear async updates | Deliver features end-to-end | Occasional peer pairing
Senior| System design at service level | Drives multiple feature launches | Influences across teams | Owns service outcomes | Regular mentor, conducts reviews
Staff | Architecture guidance | Shapes product direction | Trusted cross-functional partner | Owns long-lived initiatives | Leads mentorship programs

(Managers should consult the detailed competency maps in 02_roles-and-career.)

3) Tools & Access Matrix (common roles)
Goal: reduce repeated access requests and define expected timelines for approvals. The access matrix below is normative and should be enforced by the provisioning pipeline.
- Provisioning SLA targets:
  - Okta core accounts: 24–48 hours pre-start (automated).
  - GitHub org membership: within 24 hours of Okta provisioning.
  - 1Password vaults and secrets: 48 hours.
  - Cloud console read-only: within 72 hours after security review.

ASCII Access Matrix (role-focused)
Role | Dev Repos | Infra Console | Observability | Billing View | HRIS
Dev   | Write | No | Read | No | Self-service
Eng Lead | Write | Read | Read | Approver | Self-service
SRE   | Read | Admin | Read/Write | No | Self-service
Customer Success | Read | No | Read | Read | Self-service
People Ops | Read | No | No | Approver | Admin

Notes:
- "Approver" indicates the role can approve billing or access requests but not act as org-level owner.
- Requests requiring "Admin" on infra consoles require security review and manager sign-off.

4) Benefits & Perks Mapping (concise)
We provide a flexible benefits stack; team managers and People Ops coordinate to ensure benefits align to life stage and role.
- Core benefits (all employees): health/dental/vision, parental leave, flexible vacation, standard commuter support (where applicable).
- Perks tiers (based on employment status)
  - Full-time employees: stipend for home office, professional development allowance (USD 1,500/year), RRSP/401k matching.
  - Part-time/contractor: prorated benefits package; specific eligibility rules documented in HRIS.
  - New parents: phased return-to-work and childcare support resources via an employee assistance partner.
- Special allowances: relocation reimbursement for approved roles, education reimbursement for role-related certifications, home ergonomics stipend for hybrid contributors.

5) Hiring Handoff & First-Day Checklist (for hiring manager + People Ops)
Steps (numbered):
1. Final offer accepted -> People Ops sends welcome packet and provisioning form.
2. Manager completes team onboarding bundle and assigns buddy/mentor.
3. Provisioning pipeline triggers: Okta -> GitHub -> CI -> Monitoring dashboards. Confirm within SLA.
4. Day 0 manager message sent in Slack and calendar invites created for orientation and architecture walkthrough.
5. Completion confirmation: manager marks entry in HRIS and tags People Ops for a 30-day check-in.

6) Role Transition & Internal Mobility Flow (operational runbook)
- Initiating a move: candidate submits internal mobility request (Confluence template linked) and notifies current and target manager.
- Transition timeline: standard 4–8 weeks depending on role complexity; specialist transitions may require knowledge-transfer (KT) doc and paired weeks.
- Handover artifacts: backlog, runbook, architecture notes, access lists, and a 2-week shadow plan.
- People Ops will schedule calibration between managers and ensure compensation alignment.

7) Measurement & KPIs
Track these indicators monthly and review quarterly with People Ops and eng leadership:
- Time-to-core-access (target <= 72 hours)
- Time-to-first-meaningful-PR (target <= 14 days)
- First-90-day competence pass rate (target >= 85%)
- Internal mobility conversion time (median <= 6 weeks)

8) FAQ (short)
Q: Who is responsible for security approvals for privileged infra access?
A: Team manager and Eng-Security must co-sign; requests go through Jira workflow security-access.
Q: How do I request an exception to the provisioning SLA?
A: File a ticket to #people-ops and tag your manager; exceptions are time-boxed and recorded.
Q: Who owns the career checkpoint rubric?
A: People Ops maintains the rubric; managers and the IC-run promotion committee interpret and apply it.

9) Ownership & Escalation
- Primary owner: People Ops (Maya Patel) — content updates, quarterly reviews.
- Operational owners: Team managers (first-90-day execution) and Platform Leads (tools & access enforcement).
- Escalation path: Manager -> People Ops -> Head of People Ops -> CEO (for executive exceptions).

Appendix A — Quick CLI snippets & templates
1) Provisioning request (example):
   POST /provisioning/api/v1/requests 
   {
     \"username\": \"jlee@redwood.ai\",
     \"role_bundle\": \"eng-dev-standard\",
     \"start_date\": \"2026-08-01\"
   }
2) Internal mobility template (Confluence page): use template \"Internal Mobility Request\" and include: role rationale, expected KT, timeline, and manager confirmations.

Appendix B — Revision history
- 2026-01-12: Created (initial playbook).
- 2026-04-20: Added SLA targets for provisioning and clarified access matrix.
- 2026-09-03: Updated benefits mapping and tightened KPIs after Q2 review.

Contact & next steps
If you are a manager or new joiner with suggested improvements, open a PR against this doc or ping #people-ops-onboarding. Quarterly review due 2026-12-01.
